This Mfa Is Filed Under Section 173(1) Of Mv Act
Against The Judgment And Award Dated 03.03.2016
Passed In Mvc No.2057/14 On The File Of The Senior
Civil Judge & Mact, Beluru, Awarding Compensation
Of Rs.12,32,000/- With Interest At 9% P.A. From The
Date Of Petition Till Realization.

This Appeal, Coming On For Final Hearing, This
Day, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

In this appeal, the Insurance Company has challenged the judgment and award dated 03.03.2016 passed in M.V.C.No.2057/2014 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T., Belur (for short 'the Tribunal') in allowing the claim made by the petitioners under Section 166 of the Motor NC:
2023:KHC:40789 Vehicles Act and awarding compensation of Rs.12,32,000/- with interest at 9%
per annum.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred with respect to their status before the Tribunal.

3. Briefly stated the facts are the son of petitioner No.1, brother of petitioner Nos.2 to 6 by name Krishnamurthy, the deceased, met with an accident at 3.00 p.m. on 16.07.2014 at Bommenahalli Gate on Hassan-Belur Road while riding his motor cycle bearing No.KA-46/J-0218 hit by car The Manager vs Dyavamma on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129678916/
2 bearing No.KA-41/Z-3424 injuring him severely.

He was treated at Government Hospital, Hassan,
NIMHANS, Bangalore and again at Government Hospital, Hassan where while he was succumbed to death on 7.9.2014.
The petitioners as dependants have approached the Tribunal for compensation.
Claim was opposed by the respondents.

After taking the evidence, the Tribunal NC:
2023:KHC:40789 allowed the claim petition and awarded compensation of Rs.12,32,000/-.
Aggrieved by the same, the Insurance Company has filed this appeal on various grounds.
The Insurance Company has also filed I.A.No.1/2022 under Order XLI Rule 27 of CPC along with some documents seeking permission to produce them as additional evidence.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri.O.Mahesh, learned counsel for the Insurance Company and Sri.H.T.Jagadeesh, learned Counsel for respondent Nos.1, 2 to 4 and 6/petitioners and Sri.Rajkumar, learned Counsel for respondent No.7/owner of the car.
5.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the Insurance Company that before the Tribunal,
the petitioners have not examined any of the eyewitnesses to explain the accident.
Only on the basis of the evidence of the first petitioner, who is not an eyewitness, claim has been determined.

The NC:
2023:KHC:40789 petitioners have not proved the accident independently.
Unfortunately, there was no occasion for the Insurance Company to lead evidence before the Tribunal.
The driver of the car has been prosecuted before the learned Additional Civil Judge and JMFC., Hassan in C.C.No.9282/2014.
Before the JMFC court, all the eyewitnesses have stated specifically that they have not at all seen the accident.
The learned Magistrate has acquitted the driver of the car holding that the charge has not been proved.
The Insurance Company has a valid case on merits and sought for an opportunity to lead evidence to demonstrate the defence.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the petitioners has contended that before the Tribunal, the Insurance Company has opposed the claim by filing the objection statement.

Issues have framed and evidence was let in, as there was no rebuttal evidence, the material on record establishes the NC:
2023:KHC:40789 accident in question and for this reason, the Tribunal has awarded compensation.
Now the Insurance Company has invented a new case, mere acquittal of the driver of the car has nothing to do with the claim.
The statement of the witnesses is manipulated by the driver of the car for the sake of acquittal, which cannot be considered and sought for rejection of the application as well as the appeal.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of the parties and perused the records.
8. On perusal of the impugned judgment, the Tribunal has accepted the accident on the ground that there is no rebuttal evidence produced by the respondents.
The accident has occurred involving the motor cycle and the car.

What is the contribution of the deceased in the accident or whether it was due to sole negligence on the part of NC: 2023:KHC:40789 the driver of the car resulting in the accident has to be ascertained.

9. The material placed by the Insurance Company as additional evidence did point out that the statements given before the Magistrate by one Puttaswamy, Veerabhadra, Ravikumar, Deepak,
The Manager vs Dyavamma on 10 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129678916/
3 Mohan Kumar, Gopi, Manukumar and the Investigating Officer/A.T.Bhanu cannot be the basis for deciding this appeal.
On behalf of the petitioners only first petitioner was examined as PW-1 and no eyewitnesses are examined before the Tribunal.

The Insurance Company has taken a specific plea in the objection statement that there is a head-on collision between the motor cycle and the car and there is negligence on the part of the rider as well as the driver of the car and therefore, the petitioners are not entitled to claim compensation.
In view of the specific plea, the Tribunal is required to analyze the evidence regarding the manner of accident.
If there NC: 2023:KHC:40789 is contributory negligence on the part of the deceased and also the driver of the car, the percentage of contributory negligence has to be determined.

In the event contributory negligence is established out of total compensation, percentage of contribution has to be excluded and the petitioners are entitled for compensation only for the contributory negligence on the part of the driver of the car for which matter requires re-consideration.

At this stage, in this appeal it is not proper to appreciate the evidence given in C.C.No.9282/2014 as opportunity has to be given to both petitioners as well as the respondents to place evidence before the Tribunal regarding accident, cause of accident and regarding plea of contributory negligence.
10. In a case of this nature, the evidence adduced by the prosecution in prosecuting the driver of the car is nothing to do with the decision of the claim.

The parties have to adduce independent NC:
2023:KHC:40789 evidence in proof of the accident and the circumstances under which the witnesses have given evidence before the Criminal Court has to be brought out in the cross-examination.
Hence, the Insurance Company has made out a ground to permit them to adduce evidence and also an opportunity to the petitioners to adduce independent additional evidence in proof of the accident.
Hence, the matter requires re-consideration before the Tribunal.
It is a fit case for remand.

In the result, the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed.
ii) The impugned judgment and award is set aside.
iii) The matter is restored to the file of Tribunal to the stage of evidence.

The Tribunal shall give an opportunity to the petitioners to adduce further evidence and also to the respondents to lead evidence and then decide the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:40789 case afresh in accordance with law within six months from the date of receipt of copy of this order without being influenced by any of the observations made hereinabove.
iv) Without further notice, the parties shall appear before the Tribunal on 4th December 2023.
v) The amount in deposit, shall be  transferred to Tribunal.
